Revisitation of previously fixated locations

Source: R/revisits.R
fixation_revisits.Rd

Scores, fixation by fixation, whether gaze returns to a location already fixated earlier in the same viewing episode, and summarises each episode as counts, rates and, optionally, rates expected under a spatial reference distribution. This is a spatial-return measure related to Kragel et al. (2021), not the backtracking-sequence classification of Voss et al. (2011), which classified A-B-C-A as "other" rather than revisitation.

Usage

fixation_revisits(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fixation_group'
fixation_revisits(
  x,
  radius,
  min_lag = 2,
  max_lag = Inf,
  require_departure = TRUE,
  reference = NULL,
  dist_method = c("euclidean", "manhattan"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fixation_group or an eye_table.

...

Further arguments passed to methods.

radius

Distance within which two fixations count as the same location.

min_lag

Minimum number of fixations back for an eligible earlier fixation (default 2).

max_lag

Maximum number of fixations back, a whole number at least min_lag, or Inf (default) for no limit.

require_departure

Logical; require the preceding fixation to lie at least radius from the current fixation (default TRUE).

reference

Optional two-column matrix or data frame of x, y finite numeric locations used for the spatial reference distribution.

dist_method

"euclidean" (default) or "manhattan".

Value

For a fixation_group, a tibble with one row per fixation in onset order: index, onset, opportunity, revisit, lag (fixations back to the most recent matched fixation), match_index (that fixation's original index), nearest_distance (to the nearest eligible earlier fixation), match_distance (to match_index, which need not be nearest), distance (a compatibility alias for nearest_distance) and expected (null probability of a revisit, or NA without reference support). Distances are NA outside opportunities; match_distance is also NA without a match. Attributes retain radius, min_lag, max_lag, require_departure, dist_method and null (whether a reference was supplied). Use revisit_summary() for one row per episode. For an eye_table, see fixation_revisits.eye_table.

Details

Fixation \(i\) is a revisit when it lies within radius of at least one earlier fixation \(j\) that is at least min_lag fixations back (and at most max_lag). The default min_lag = 2 means a fixation never revisits the fixation immediately before it. With require_departure = TRUE (default), the incoming step must be at least radius: the preceding fixation must lie at least radius away from fixation \(i\). This does not require leaving and re-entering a region centred on the earlier fixation. For example, with radius 10, positions 0, -9, 9 on one axis count as a return, although both later positions are within radius of the original position. A fixation is an opportunity when it could have been a revisit: it has an eligible earlier fixation and, under require_departure, arrives from at least radius away.

Revisit counts rise mechanically when an observer makes many fixations within a small area, so raw counts partly restate fixation number and spatial dispersion. Supplying reference locations gives a spatial null: for each opportunity, the expected probability of a revisit is the proportion of reference locations that would count as a revisit of the same eligible earlier fixations, among those reference locations that also satisfy the departure condition. A natural reference is the observer's fixations from other trials, which preserves the observer's spatial bias but not the order within the episode (see the eye_table method, null = "subject"). Observed minus expected is a descriptive correction under this reference distribution, not an inferential test or a generative model of scanpaths.

Coordinates and onsets must be finite numeric values. Invalid values cause an error; dropping fixations would change adjacency, lags and denominators. Fixations are scored in onset order, preserving input order for tied onsets. Lag bounds are whole numbers; large finite bounds are supported without conversion to 32-bit integers.

Reference coverage is updated as fixations enter and leave the eligible lag window. For \(n\) fixations, \(m\) reference points and maximum eligible history size \(L\), scoring uses \(O(n + nL + nm)\) time and \(O(n + m)\) storage, including result rows. No pairwise distance matrix is allocated.

radius is in the units of the fixation coordinates. Kragel et al. (2021) used about 2 degrees of visual angle; convert degrees to pixels for your display geometry before calling.

References

Voss, J. L., Warren, D. E., Gonsalves, B. D., Federmeier, K. D., Tranel, D., & Cohen, N. J. (2011). Spontaneous revisitation during visual exploration as a link among strategic behavior, learning, and the hippocampus. PNAS, 108(31), E402-E409.

Kragel, J. E., Schuele, S., VanHaerents, S., Rosenow, J. M., & Voss, J. L. (2021). Rapid coordination of effective learning by the human hippocampus. Science Advances, 7(25), eabf7144.

Examples

# A-B-C-A: the fourth fixation returns to the first location
fg <- fixation_group(x = c(100, 400, 400, 105), y = c(100, 100, 400, 98),
                     onset = c(0, 250, 500, 750), duration = rep(200, 4))
rv <- fixation_revisits(fg, radius = 50)
rv
#> Revisits: 1 of 2 opportunities (4 fixations; radius 50, lag 2-Inf, departure required)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 10
#>   index onset opportunity revisit   lag match_index distance nearest_distance
#>   <int> <dbl> <lgl>       <lgl>   <int>       <int>    <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1     1     0 FALSE       FALSE      NA          NA    NA               NA   
#> 2     2   250 FALSE       FALSE      NA          NA    NA               NA   
#> 3     3   500 TRUE        FALSE      NA          NA   424.             424.  
#> 4     4   750 TRUE        TRUE        3           1     5.39             5.39
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: match_distance <dbl>, expected <dbl>
revisit_summary(rv)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   n_fix opportunities revisits revisit_rate expected_revisits expected_rate
#>   <int>         <int>    <int>        <dbl>             <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1     4             2        1          0.5                NA            NA
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: excess_revisits <dbl>, excess_rate <dbl>
